findings.title: Unrelated git undo commands are attributed to preceding file edits
findings.what: The undo branch requires only a file-edit call with a nonempty path followed within three calls by any Bash command matching git checkout/restore/revert/reset. Although curFile is computed, it is never compared with the undo command's target. Editing /a.ts followed by git restore /b.ts therefore increments immediatelyFollowedByUndo for the /a.ts edit and lowers its effectiveness score without evidence that the edit was reverted.
findings.fix: Parse or precompute the undo command's affected paths and set sawUndo only when the current edit path is among them; suppress attribution when target provenance is absent or ambiguous.
findings.acceptance: Add a test with Edit(file_path=/a.ts) followed by git restore /b.ts and assert immediatelyFollowedByUndo is 0, while the existing same-path /a.ts case remains 1 and its score remains 0.5.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read at baseline confirmed curFile is only checked for non-null at lines 203-224; isUndoBash at lines 63-69 returns only a command-kind boolean and exposes no target comparison. The existing test covers only a matching path.

findings.title: API errors are rescanned and resorted for every session
findings.what: sessionApiErrorTimes iterates the entire apiErrors array and sorts the matching subset, and computeToolEffectiveness invokes it once for every tool-data session. With S sessions and E errors this performs O(S×E) filtering work plus repeated sorts during ingest.
findings.fix: Build a Map<sessionId, number[]> from apiErrors once before the session loop, sort each session bucket once, and perform constant-time bucket lookup inside the loop.
findings.acceptance: Add a scale-oriented unit or benchmark fixture with many sessions and errors, instrument error-record visits, and assert each API error is indexed once while all effectiveness rows remain identical.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read at the pinned baseline confirmed lines 82-87 scan and sort the supplied global array, and line 171 calls that function inside the per-session loop; no pre-indexed error map exists.
